title: Injective increasing-tuple row augmentation
statement: Let X be a scheme, U:Fin r→X.Opens an open cover, and M an injective O_X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. There exists a morphism from the integer single complex of global sections in degree zero to the explicit increasing-tuple alternatingCechModuleFunctor(U)(M) [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex]. Its zero component is singleObjXSelf.hom followed by alternatingCechZero U M, and this very morphism is a quasi-isomorphism. No coefficient complex or totalization occurs in this assertion.

source.place: First paragraph, row exactness from Tags 01EP and 01FM.

proof.text: Construct the canonical nonnegative augmentation using fromSingle₀Equiv. Its differential vanishes by cancellation of the two face restrictions of a global section. Sheaf gluing gives a preimage for any zero-degree cocycle: evaluate on an increasing pair to show the singleton sections agree, reversing the pair for the opposite order. Sheaf separatedness proves injectivity, including empty covers. Identify the top scalar restriction with the identity. The degree-zero quasi-isomorphism criterion now applies.

Construct SiteCechComplex with genuine finite intersections and homOfLE maps. Forget the global-ring scalars of the actual alternating row. Construct the cochain map evaluating a full cochain on each embedding, and identify strictly monotone functions with order embeddings. The signed face formulas commute with restriction. Apply the existing alternatingCechRestrictionHomotopy to get a homotopy equivalence. The full-tuple row has zero positive homology for an injective module by module_injective_open_cover_cech_acyclic, hence the alternating abelian row is exact. The elementwise abelian-group and module exactness criteria agree.

The single complex is exact outside degree zero, so degree-zero comparison and positive exactness make the constructed nonnegative augmentation a quasi-isomorphism. Extend it by zero along embeddingUpNat, precompose with extendSingleIso.inv, and compute the zero component using extendMap_f and extendSingleIso_inv_f. It is singleObjXSelf.hom followed by alternatingCechZero. Extension and isomorphisms preserve quasi-isomorphisms.

theorem injective_alternatingCech_row_augmentation
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (r : ℕ) (U : Fin r → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) [Injective M] :
    ∃ f : (HomologicalComplex.single
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
        ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).obj M) ⟶
          (alternatingCechModuleFunctor U).obj M,
      f.f 0 = (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0
        ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).obj M)).hom ≫
          alternatingCechZero U M ∧ QuasiIso f
